Definition: properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling
BiblicalUsage: A generation, the circle of people alive at one time, and the measure of God's memory: He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and this is His name for ever, unto all generations. The Amorites' iniquity would not be full until the fourth generation, and one generation passes away while another comes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God keeps His promises across generations, because His name is the same to my children's children as it was to Abraham. One generation passes and another comes, but the earth abides and the God of the generations abides with it.
